title: FEHA source-of-income and criminal-history screening protections
requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent based on a tenant's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers, and may not impose blanket criminal-history bans or consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records.
coverage_conditions: Applies to most housing accommodations in California, including single-family and multi-family homes, apartments, condominiums, short-term rentals, mobile homes, subsidized housing, dormitories, sober living, group homes, shelters, and RVs or boats used as homes.

applicability.per_tenancy: An owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics; a shared single dwelling may be limited to one sex; housing for seniors or homeless youth may be limited by age.

exemptions: Owner-occupied home renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics; senior housing and homeless youth housing may be limited by age; a shared single dwelling may be limited to one sex.
penalty: Remedies include recovery of out-of-pocket losses, an injunction, access to the housing denied, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
citation: California's Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: No. California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job.
